record.paper_title: Some Open Questions in Quiver Gauge Theory
record.original_question: Brane tilings carry a modular parameter tau_R coming from isoradial embedding and R-charges, while the associated Belyi pair defines a modular parameter tau_B. In which situations does the equality tau_B = tau_R hold?

evidence.quote: Question 23. In what scenarios does τB = τR hold?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A brane tiling is a bipartite graph drawn on a two-dimensional torus that encodes the data of a four-dimensional N=1 superconformal quiver gauge theory associated with a toric Calabi–Yau threefold. Two complex structures (modular parameters of the torus) can be attached to such a tiling:

(1) The R-charge modular parameter τ_R. By a-maximization, every chiral field of the gauge theory acquires an R-charge R_i ∈ (0,1). An isoradial embedding of the brane tiling places every edge as a chord of a unit circle so that the angle subtended at each white/black node by the edge corresponding to a field of R-charge R_i equals πR_i. The fundamental domain of this embedding is a parallelogram in the plane whose ratio of sides (with the appropriate orientation) defines a point τ_R in the upper half-plane, well-defined modulo SL(2,Z).

(2) The Belyi modular parameter τ_B. The combinatorial data of the brane tiling (its permutation triple, or equivalently the associated dessin d'enfant on the torus) determines a Belyi pair (E, β), where E is an elliptic curve and β : E → P^1 is a holomorphic map ramified only over {0, 1, ∞}. The complex structure of E gives a modular parameter τ_B in the upper half-plane, well-defined modulo SL(2,Z).

Problem: Characterize the brane tilings (equivalently, the toric Calabi–Yau threefolds and their associated dessins d'enfants on the torus) for which the equality τ_B = τ_R holds in SL(2,Z)\H. In particular, identify necessary and sufficient combinatorial or geometric conditions on the brane tiling that guarantee this equality.
artifact.status_search_result: Related literature (notably work on "the beta ansatz" and on dessins d'enfants for quiver gauge theories) discusses the comparison between the Belyi complex structure τ_B and the isoradial/R-charge complex structure τ_R and notes agreement in special examples (e.g. certain Z_n orbifolds), but a general characterization of when τ_B = τ_R remains an open question, with the precise relationship between Belyi algebraic data, R-charges, and Sasaki–Einstein volumes still not understood.

status_evidence.title: The beta ansatz: a tale of two complex structures
status_evidence.snippet: Two complex structures arise in brane tilings: one from the isoradial embedding determined by R-charges, the other from the associated Belyi pair; the relationship between them is investigated.
status_evidence.claim: Comparison of τ_R and τ_B is an active research question with only special-case agreements known.

status_evidence.title: Gauge Theories and Dessins d'Enfants: Beyond the Torus
status_evidence.snippet: How algebraic numbers in the Belyi pair precisely relate to the R-charges (under isoradial embedding) and to volumes in the dual Sasaki-Einstein geometry remains to be understood.
status_evidence.claim: The general relationship between Belyi data and R-charges is stated as not yet understood.
